commitResults.messageBody:
Chatbot is to be differentiated from placeholder name Duke. Renamed all
instances of Duke to Bern and updated ASCII Banner art to reflect name
changes.

Chatbot name is to be differentiable so separate submissions of the iP
by different students can be more easily identified by the teaching
team.

Let's rename every instance of Duke to Bern and update the ASCII Banner
art to reflect this change.

Bern, a.k.a. Bern Tokens, is a reference to AI agents burning tokens.

The chatbot currently does not greet the user and say goodbye on exit.

This makes the chatbot feel less friendly.

A greeting and exit message have been added with templates.

The templates make it easier for changes to be made to these messages if needed.

Access modifier for chatbot banner is public.

This causes unintended access.

Access modifier has been changed to private.

Chatbot does not do anything.

Chatbot should do something.

Added ability for chatbot to repeatedly echo commands from user input.
Chatbot exits when user inputs "bye" (case insensitive).

This gives the chatbot something to do instead of quitting out
immediately.

Echoed input is stripped before being printed to standard output.

commitResults.messageTitle: Fix chatbot behaviour on empty inputs
commitResults.messageBody:
Chatbot will echo stripped inputs that are completely empty.

This is pointless since the user will see the bot respond with nothing.

Chatbot will now not echo the given input until it receives an input
string that is non-empty after stripping.

This is so the bot will only respond once actual inputs are given.

Current chatbot can only echo commands.

Chatbot should be more useful.

Chatbot can now keep track of up to 100 tasks that the user can input.
User can list these tasks thorugh the "list" command (case insensitive).

Chatbot now is able to better serve a purpose (in this case, a way for
users to store tasks)

No way to mark tasks as complete.

This limits the utility of the bot, especially when there are a
combination of tasks that are both complete and incomplete. Users will
not be able to conveniently track which tasks have already been
completed.

Let's make it such that tasks can now be marked or unmarked. Command is
"mark [task number]" to mark a task and "unmark [task number]" to
unmark a task. Invalid task numbers and other inputs are not accepted.

This is so users can better keep track of their task progress.

This commit contains significant code duplication between the mark and
unmark branches in the main() function. This should be reviewed to see
how code can be made cleaner.

Printing of messages to standard output is tedious due to the constant
need to add "\n" + MESSAGE_LINE.

This makes code more difficult to write and change.

Let's add a printMessage() function to auotmatically execute this
behaviour.

This makes printing of messages easier to read.

commitResults.messageTitle: Differentiate Tasks into Todo, Deadline and Event
commitResults.messageBody:
Current chatbot can collect tasks and list them.

This is limited in the sense that it cannot differentiate between the
different kinds of tasks, especially those that are time-specific.

Let's add three kinds of tasks:
* Todo: A task with no deadline. Command: todo <task>
* Deadline: A task with a deadline. Command: deadline <task> /by
  <deadline>
* Event: An event with a start and end time. Command: event <task> /from
  <start time> /to <end time>

This allows for better visualisation of the tasks at hand and which ones
may be more urgent.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add basic error handling for some commands
commitResults.messageBody:
Commands do not handle incorrect inputs.

This causes the program to hit runtime exceptions and expose the stack
trace to the user.

Let's add exception handling so the program catches incorrect inputs and
notifies the user accordingly.

This results in a more user-friendly experience.

commitResults.messageTitle: Rework keyword detection and parse logic
commitResults.messageBody:
Keyword detection and parse logic is messy and difficult to read.

This makes it challenging to edit and update.

Let's rework the logic using an enum and abstracting away the long
chunks of code in the switch block.

This makes the code easier to read.

Tasks cannot be deleted and will permanently remain in the chatbot's
logs.

This means that tasks will eventually pile up with no way to remove
them.

Let's add a way to remove tasks through the remove command. Syntax:
remove <task number>.

This helps clean up tasks that are complete.

commitResults.messageTitle: Refine use of Enums in the program
commitResults.messageBody:
Keyword enum used to navigate lengthy switch block.

This is a little hard to read still and could be further optimised to
reduce code bloat.

Let's add a Consumer field to each enum. When a keyword is detected the
Consumer is called. Using the Command design pattern we can simplify the
code in main() since it no longer needs to worry about execution logic.

This makes code significantly easier to read and edit.

One small caveat is that Keyword.BYE still needs to flip the boolean for
isReadingInput from true to false. A better solution would be preferred,
but currently the check for Keyword.BYE is done one more time outside of
the action.

Chatbot forgets all tasks after exiting.

This makes the chatbot less useful for tasks that may have deadlines or
start and end times that are very far in the future since the program is
unlikely to be kept running indefinitely.

Let's
* Save existing tasks on the bye command into a text file with file path
  ./data/tasks.txt
* Add a SaveDataController to manage save data
* Add the ./data/ directory to .gitignore to avoid committing irrelevant
  test data when committing
* Add methods for each Task class (and its subclasses) that convert
  their stored data into an ArrayList<> for SaveDataController to
  process
* Add a method to TaskFactory to build the various Task types from the
  saved data parsed by SaveDataController

This allows save data to persist between chatbot use sessions, making it
more useful for long-term tasks.

No save functionality implemented so far.

This means all progress is lost when the bot is closed.

Let's merge to confirm save functionality.

This allows the bot to be more useful by being able to store deadlines
that are further into the future without forgetting them on exit.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add date and time validation for tasks.
commitResults.messageBody:
Tasks (specifically Deadlines and Todos) do not validate date and time
inputs.

This makes it difficult to organise or filter dates by time.

Let's
* Split functionality of the TaskFactory class into a ParseFactory
  superclass
* Use the ParseFactory superclass to make a DateTimeFactory subclass
* Make a DateTime class to encapsulate a LocalDate and LocalTime
* Store the date and time in the new DateTime format

This allows us to perform operations on tasks based on dates.

commitResults.messageTitle: Fix oversight on saving date formats
commitResults.messageBody:
Reading from save data will fail due to oversight when updating save
data format.

This causes the program to reject reading the save data and start from a
fresh state, which is not intentional.

Let's fix this bug and implement proper functionality in DateTime and
DateTimeFactory to save task dates and times properly.

This fixes the aforementioned bug.

commitResults.messageTitle: Allow parsing of date time through time alone
commitResults.messageBody:
Inputting tasks such as deadline /by 5.00pm will fail since no date is
specify.

Intuitively, this does not make sense and it is a hassle to constantly
type out the current date.

Let's allow the bot to parse such inputs by taking the date as the
current date on the user's system time.

This makes it easier to input multiple tasks on the current date.

Add date time functionality to the chatbot.

This date time functionality allows tasks to be processed with respect
to the timings that they occur/are due by.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract task-management code to its own class
commitResults.messageBody:
Bern class serves multiple functions.

This makes code harder to write and edit.

Let's extract code relating to task management into its own TaskManager
class.

This isolates the task management code to be contained within its own
structure and reduces coupling at the same time.

commitResults.messageTitle: Restructure message printing to Ui class
commitResults.messageBody:
Main Bern class handles printing to console.

Bern handles other behaviour, which can cause the Bern class to become
convoluted.

Let's
* Extract Ui into its own class and apply the Singleton pattern
* Move most printMessage calls into their own respective methods
* Remove "magic numbers" and turn them into constants in the Ui class

This reduces code bloat in Bern.java

Bern is a "god class" that handles multiple behaviours.

Let's extract functionality of the TaskList and Ui into their own
individual classes.

This reduces code bloat in Bern.java and allows code to be more
readable.

Class files are currently all not organised.

This causes some confusion when navigating the directory, and will pose
more significant problems as the size of the code base increases.

Let's make separate packages that categorise each class by its
functionality.

This creates clear distinctions between classes and also controls how
much access these classes have to other methods.

All files are in the same directory with no organisation.

This makes it more difficult to locate files, especially when more
classes are added afterwards due to increased project size.

Let's organise files into packages according to what function they
serve.

This makes file navigation easier when editing code, especially when
project size increases later on.

Project build is not yet automated.

This means building can sometimes be a hassle.

Let's merge 'add-gradle-support' as part of the requirement to A-Gradle.

This allows us to automate project builds.

commitResults.messageTitle: Update Gradle-related files to support project
commitResults.messageBody:
Gradle files are based on an earlier commit where Duke was used.

The project is no longer named Duke, and hence the build.gradle file
must be updated.

Let's
* Update the build.gradle file to reflect the name changes
* Add support to run the checkstyle plugin for future use

This allows us to develop with more convenience later on.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add JUnit Tests for DateTime and ParseFactory
commitResults.messageBody:
There are no tests written at the moment.

This means when software changes, old code may break without convenient
ways to verify which functionality has failed.

Let's:
* Add a DateTimeTest class which tests if DateTime performs correctly
  with nullary Time fields
* Add a ParseFactoryTest which tests if ParseFactory performs correctly
  with empty keyword arrays and throws exceptions correctly when there
  are no arguments supplied after each keyword

This helps to ensure that critical functionality can be easily tested
and verify that these functions are working even after changes in code.

There are no JUnit tests.

Testing is a vital part of SWE and should not be omitted.

Let's add some testing to the classes to rectify this.

This allows us to more conveniently verify that new changes do not
breake existing functionality.
